key_insight: Returning only optimal decisions can still expose a linear prediction model up to positive scaling, motivating a defense that perturbs decisions near decision boundaries.
engineering_relevance: Predict-then-optimize APIs should treat decision outputs as potential model-leakage channels and balance extraction resistance against optimization regret.
method: Establish sufficient conditions for recovering linear models from decision-only queries.
Construct an adaptive attack alternating inverse optimization with boundary-focused context queries.
Perturb decisions near cost-space decision boundaries, with regret and conditional extraction-error guarantees.
evidence_signal: Experiments on synthetic instances and real data quantify the security–performance trade-off and show that the defense can increase extraction error.
watch_item: The extraction-error lower bound applies to attackers that fit defended responses as optimal decisions under the evaluation distribution, not necessarily all attack strategies.
paper_title: Preventing Model Extraction in Contextual Linear Optimization
